trust_decision.summary: The server must not fetch private/internal addresses on behalf of a client: every URL posted to the proxy route has to have its destination address (after DNS resolution) validated before the server-side fetch; the check is decided at src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:9, and the second fix commit moves the decision into a connection-time agent at fix.diff:141.

landing_point.why: The advisory names /api/proxy; the POST body is read as a raw URL string and passed straight to fetch with no destination check, which is exactly the code an engineer who read only the summary would open first.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/proxy (called from the browser by src/services/tool.ts:17 and src/services/file/client.ts:23)
fix_sites.module_kind: Next.js App Router route handler; edge runtime at the pinned commit, switched to nodejs by the fix so node:dns can be used

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /webapi/proxy (new location introduced by fix commit e960a23b; the old src/app/api/proxy/route.ts is deleted at fix.diff:84-123)
fix_sites.module_kind: Next.js App Router route handler using node-fetch plus request-filtering-agent (connection-time address filtering, follows redirects safely)

fix_sites.entry_point: client API_ENDPOINTS map (proxy: '/api/proxy' changed to '/webapi/proxy' at fix.diff:176-177), consumed by src/services/tool.ts:17 and src/services/file/client.ts:23

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The other server-side fetch routes are each an intentional feature the user configures (the chat provider endpoint is the user's own BYOK/Ollama base URL; /api/files/image is the Imgur upload helper; the plugin gateway exists to call remote plugin servers), so a solver can argue they are not the /api/proxy SSRF and leave them open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Fetching plugin manifests and images from plain-http, localhost or LAN hosts through the proxy is a supported use: the plugin dev form only requires ^https?://, the proxy exists precisely to bypass CORS for plugin manifests, and self-hosted users host plugins/images on internal addresses; a blanket private-address or non-https block (or refusing any redirect) breaks plugin install and local plugin development.

O6_input_shapes: raw URL string sent as the request body text (not JSON)
host that is a DNS name requiring resolution vs an IP literal
IPv4 private/loopback/link-local literals rejected via ip.isPrivate (fix.diff:57)
hostname that resolves to a private address, e.g. 127.0.0.1.nip.io (handled by the first commit's dns.lookup, fix.diff:49-60)
redirect whose target is a private address (handled only by the second commit's request-filtering-agent, fix.diff:141)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/files/image fetches the 'url' field of the JSON body server-side and uploads the response to Imgur, with no address validation
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the Imgur image-upload helper, not the proxy: the fetched body is not returned to the caller (blind) and the URL is the image the user is saving
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different feature directory from the landing point (src/app/api/files vs src/app/api/proxy), 2 files

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/chat/[provider] takes the client-supplied 'endpoint' from the auth JWT payload as the provider baseURL and lets the OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/Ollama/Azure SDK fetch it, including private addresses
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A custom provider endpoint is a first-class BYOK/Ollama feature and self-hosters legitimately point it at localhost or a LAN host, so it is intended configuration rather than the proxy flaw

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/plugin/gateway delegates to createGatewayOnEdgeRuntime, which fetches the plugin API endpoint named by the client-supplied manifest/payload; the client even chooses the gateway URL via manifest.gateway
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Plugins are remote services by design and the route already requires a LOBE_CHAT_AUTH_HEADER token, so fetching a caller-named plugin URL is the feature itself

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second server-side 'fetch a user-supplied URL' helper for image import
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding image-by-URL import writes a small route that fetches the URL itself instead of reusing the proxy, exactly as this route already does; it sits in a different feature directory from the proxy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A provider endpoint passthrough that hands a caller-chosen baseURL to an outbound HTTP client
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Adding self-hosted/proxy endpoint support for each new model provider is a routine contribution, and no author would think to apply an SSRF filter to a user's own configured endpoint.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A manifest whose 'openapi' field points at a second URL that is then fetched (src/services/tool.ts:84)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plugin manifests legitimately reference an OpenAPI document by URL, so a maintainer naturally follows the second URL from the first response, letting a manifest chain the server to another destination.

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm scripts (next build/next dev, tsc --noEmit); vitest ~1.2.2 for tests; no lockfile present in this tree, node_modules not installed

j.j_sites_touched: src/app/api/proxy/route.ts, src/app/webapi/proxy/route.ts (new), src/services/_url.ts; unrelated drive-by in the same fix commit: src/services/user/client.ts and src/server/routers/lambda/user.ts (canEnablePWAGuide 2 -> 4)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an isPrivate()/localhost string check on the parsed URL hostname inside /api/proxy only, leave redirects and the other server-side fetch routes untouched, and stop.

out_of_scope_notes: No out-of-scope issue was pursued. Informational: fix commit e960a23b sweeps unrelated non-security changes (canEnablePWAGuide threshold 2 -> 4 in src/server/routers/lambda/user.ts and src/services/user/client.ts); those are not security fix sites.

Note for route reachability, not pursued further: src/app/api/chat/auth/utils.ts:12-17 base64-decodes any token prefixed with 'http_nosafe' without signature verification, which makes the client-supplied JWT 'endpoint' directly attacker-controlled on plain-HTTP deployments.
